_meta.what_this_is: Five retrieved chunks with their relevance scores, and the attention profile of the five context slots they will be placed into. The slot_weights are U-shaped -- high at the two edges (start and end of the context), lowest in the exact middle -- which is the empirical 'lost in the middle' finding for long-context models. Effective information for a placement is the sum over slots of the chunk's relevance times the slot's attention.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The relevances and the U-shaped slot weights are hand-authored so the naive (relevance-order) and edge-aware (best-at-edges) placements, and their effective-information scores, are exact and checkable. Every placement and score is computed in middle.py from these numbers. Chunks are indexed c0..c4 by their order here; relevances[i] is chunk ci's relevance.
_meta.format: relevances: chunk relevance scores (index = chunk id); slot_weights: per-position attention (index = slot), U-shaped.
